issues.legal_issue: A respondent who has not appealed or filed a cross-objection may support the decree on grounds decided against it below but may not use that power to challenge the decree.
material_facts: The landholder appealed the Collector’s order on several grounds but did not challenge the finding that allotted him a specified number of land units.
The State did not appeal or file a cross-objection and submitted to the Collector’s order.
The Commissioner set aside the Collector’s order, including the unchallenged finding about the land units.
issues.conclusion: The Commissioner could not reverse the finding in the landholder’s favour under Order XLI, Rule 22, because the State had filed neither an appeal nor a cross-objection.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XLI, Rule 22(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a respondent may support a decree on grounds decided in its favour or against it, but may challenge the decree only by appeal or cross-objection. Rule 49 of the Bihar Land Reforms Rules, 1963 made Order XLI applicable to appeals under the land-reform scheme.

predicates.appellate_proceeding: The matter is an appeal in which the applicable procedure permits a respondent to support or challenge the decision under review.
predicates.respondent_filed_no_appeal_or_cross_obje: The respondent filed neither an appeal nor a cross-objection against the decision under review.
predicates.appellate_court_reversed_unappealed_favo: The appellate court reversed a finding favorable to the appealing party that the appellant had not challenged.
predicates.respondent_cannot_challenge_decree_witho: A respondent without an appeal or cross-objection cannot use the power to support a decision to challenge it.

issues.definition: When an appellate court reverses an unchallenged favorable finding in a proceeding where the respondent filed no appeal or cross-objection, the respondent cannot use the power to support the decision as a means of challenging it.

issues.legal_issue: The appellate court’s power to grant relief to a party who has not appealed must be used cautiously and does not ordinarily permit reopening a final finding unless consequential interference is necessary to adjust the parties’ rights.
material_facts: The landholder appealed on grounds other than the Collector’s finding about the allotted land units.
The State did not appeal or file a cross-objection, and the finding about the units had become final as against the State.
The Commissioner set aside that finding even though the landholder’s appeal did not make interference with it necessary to adjust the parties’ rights.
The other grounds were remanded for reconsideration, and the finding about the units could remain intact without producing an inconsistent or unworkable result.
issues.conclusion: The circumstances did not justify exercising the power under Order XLI, Rule 33 to disturb the final finding; the Commissioner and High Court erred in doing so.
issues.legal_principle: Order XLI, Rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure empowers an appellate court to make a decree or order needed to do complete justice, including relief for a party who has not appealed. The power is broad but must be exercised with care and caution; it does not permit reopening a final decree merely because the appellate court disagrees with the lower court. Ordinarily, further interference is justified where relief to the appellant makes it necessary to adjust the parties’ rights or avoid inconsistent or unworkable decisions. The Court relied on Nirmala Bala Ghose v. Balai Chand Ghose and Giani Ram v. Ramji Lal.

predicates.appellate_proceeding: The matter is an appeal in which the appellate court has power to grant relief to a party who did not appeal.
predicates.finding_became_final_without_opposing_ap: A finding became final because the party against whom it operated did not appeal or file a cross-objection.
predicates.interference_not_needed_to_adjust_rights: Changing the finding is not necessary to adjust the parties’ rights as a consequence of relief granted to the appealing party.
predicates.no_inconsistent_or_unworkable_result_wit: Leaving the finding undisturbed would not produce inconsistent or unworkable decisions.
predicates.appellate_court_may_not_reopen_final_fin: The appellate court may not reopen a final finding merely because it disagrees with that finding.

issues.definition: If a finding became final without an opposing appeal, changing it is not necessary to adjust the parties’ rights, and leaving it intact would not cause inconsistent or unworkable results, the appellate court may not reopen it merely because it disagrees with it.
